subject: possible bug in geom_point() or geom_point() documentation

messages.author: 9e8f9b870a2e6cdf
messages.subject: possible bug in geom_point() or geom_point() documentation
parts:
Hi,

Today I was using geom_point() and the documentation for this seems
to suggest that one can use, geom_point( aes( fill=some_var ) ), as
fill is listed as one of the aesthetics on http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_point.html

A sample program would be:

require(ggplot2)
dfm <- data.frame( xx = runif( 20 ),
yy = runif( 20 ),
f = factor( round( 4*runif(20), 0 ) ) )
p <- ggplot( dfm, aes( x=xx,
y=yy,
fill=f ) ) + geom_point( size=5 )

This creates, however, a graph with black points, instead of coloured
points.
Although the scale on the right shows nicely coloured points with a
black edge.

An aes( colour=f ) does work.
But the other geom's seem to suggest that colour is supposed to be for
the border.

For instance:
ggplot( dfm, aes(x=round(xx,1),y=round(yy,1),fill=f)) +
geom_tile( colour="black" )
creates coloured tiles with a black border.

Am I misunderstanding something, or is this a bug in the
implementation or documentation.

Frans.

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: possible bug in geom_point() or geom_point() documentation
parts:
Hi Frans,
Points are special in that they come in different shapes. If you use a
hollow shape for the points then fill aesthetics do indeed work. If
you use solid shapes than color is applied to the whole thing and fill
does not show up.

HTH,
Ista

messages.subject: Re: possible bug in geom_point() or geom_point() documentation
parts:
Hi, Ista is right, and please see 'pch' values section in ?points for
more details.
You can use different fill and border color for the shape #21-#25.

ggplot(data.frame(x=1:25,y=1:25,z=1:25),aes(x,y,shape=z,fill=26-z,colour=z))+geom_point(size=5)

--

Research Center for Advanced Science and Technology,
The University of  Tokyo, Japan.
http://www.fennel.rcast.u-tokyo.ac.jp/profilee_ktakahashi.html
